validity.recommendation: none — row is correctly scoped as the GTN Xpress compressor-upgrade project, distinct from the GTN system row P0231
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE: P3171 is a real, FERC-certificated project. TC PipeLines LP announced GTN XPress 2019-11-01 (globenewswire, WebFetch-confirmed: 'up to 250,000 Dth/d of additional firm transportation service', ~$335M, Kingsgate ID-to-Malin OR system). The scope was reduced to 150,000 Dth/d (150 MMcf/d) by the time of the FERC application (EIA Applied vintages from 2021-10 carry 150 MMcf/d, matching the sheet). FERC Docket CP22-2: Order Issuing Certificate 185 FERC P61,035 issued 2023-10-23 (confirmed directly from the FERC compliance-filing letterhead at the Owner/Construction ref, and independently reported by bendbulletin.com 2023-10-20 'received approval ... on Thursday morning'). GTN accepted the certificate 2024-01-30, commenced construction 2024-07-26, and by 2024-11-13 was finishing the Kent Compressor Station auxiliary facilities (targeting Nov-Dec 2024 completion); EIA's Aug2026 release marks the project 'Completed' with completed_date 2024-11-01. This is a genuine COMPRESSION-ONLY expansion of the existing GTN system (bendbulletin: 'The project won't change the structure of the existing pipeline. Instead, it will involve upgrades to three compressor stations in Athol, Idaho; Kent, Oregon; and Starbuck, Washington.') -- not a new pipeline segment, and not a duplicate of any other roster row. It is correctly kept separate from P0231 (the GTN system row, swept in another batch): P3171 is the Xpress project specifically. No existence, duplicate, or classification concern.

validity.recommendation: update SegmentCost to $335,000,000 (2023) -- the recorded $75,000,000 is a stale/superseded estimate
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's SegmentCost ($75,000,000, 2023) is materially wrong for that year. EIA's own project-cost field for GTN XPress shows $75.1M ONLY in the 2021-10 and 2022-01 releases (an early FERC-application-era estimate); every release from 2022-10 through 2026-08 -- spanning the entire period from before FERC approval through project completion -- carries $335M. Two sources independent of EIA corroborate $335M for the certificated/current-era project: (1) TC PipeLines LP's original 2019-11-01 announcement already cited ~$335M for the broader program (globenewswire, WebFetch-confirmed); (2) bendbulletin.com, reporting the 2023-10-19 FERC certificate order, states 'TC Energy, proposed ... a $335 million project to increase the capacity of the pipeline.' The current [ref] cited for SegmentCost, canadianenergycentre.ca (published 2023-11-24, AFTER the FERC order and AFTER bendbulletin's $335M report), states 'the US$75 million GTN Xpress project' -- this appears to be the outdated $75.1M FERC-application-era estimate carried over in error by that article, not a genuine restatement of the approved project's cost. The recorded $75M/2023 pairing is inconsistent with every other source dated at or after the 2023 certificate order.

validity.recommendation: verify Kent Compressor Station's state against the FERC CP22-2 order text or NPMS before treating EndState/Province as fully settled
validity.researcher_notes: The Location [ref]'s recorded StartLocation=Athol/Idaho, EndLocation=Kent/Oregon match bendbulletin.com (2023-10-20, citing a TC Energy-provided map): 'upgrades to three compressor stations in Athol, Idaho; Kent, Oregon; and Starbuck, Washington.' The project's three physical work sites can't fit GEM's two-endpoint schema, so Athol (ID) and Kent (OR) are being used as the outer bounds, omitting the middle station (Starbuck, WA) -- a schema limitation, not an error, and consistent with bendbulletin's per-station state breakdown. However, missoulacurrent.com (2022-11, a different independent outlet) describes 'the Starbuck and Kent compressor stations in Washington state' -- grouping Kent with Starbuck in WA rather than OR. I could not resolve this directly: the Federal Register EIS notice for this docket (cited on gem.wiki) returned an unblock/bot-challenge page both via curl (500) and WebFetch (redirected to unblock.federalregister.gov), and desmog.com's coverage names three stations generically without identifying them. Given bendbulletin is the Oregon-based, more detailed, map-sourced account, I am not changing the cell, but the conflict is real and unresolved -- a check of the FERC order text itself (elibrary.ferc.gov, Docket CP22-2) would settle it.
